us13_wages.topic: Minimum wage over time, hours, leave and pay gaps, Israel and US

claims.text: EPI: the 1968 federal minimum ($1.60) was worth $12.50 in 2023 dollars; $7.25 was worth $10.33 in 2023 dollars; in 2023 the real value was at a 66-year low, 42% below the 1968 peak and about 30% below its value when last raised; 30 states and DC set higher minimums.

Ballotpedia (12 Dec 2025): 22 states and DC raise minimums in 2026 (19 on 1 Jan); average state minimum $11.18 (2025) to $11.51 (2026); 20 states use the federal $7.25; 30 above it; highest DC $17.95 (July 2025).
Contradiction resolved: WageIndicator's NIS 6,247.67 'from 1 April 2026' is the 1 April 2025 rate per NII; the 2026 rate is NIS 6,443.85 (+3.1%).

Kol-Zchut: Israel's Minimum Wage Law was passed in 1987; the monthly minimum is 47.5% of the average wage, updated each 1 April; hourly = 1/186 of monthly; covers all workers including foreign and undocumented workers; reduced youth rates; employer who fails to pay faces up to a year in prison or a fine.
Taub Center (July 2010): Israel's minimum (NIS 3,850 since 2008) was 58% of the median wage, vs OECD average 46% and US 34% (23 countries); Israel 'not a strict enforcer'.

OECD average annual hours actually worked per worker (Wikipedia table): Israel 1,904 (1990), 2,033 (2000), 1,957 (2010), 1,783 (2020), 1,870 (2025); US 1,816 (1980), 1,833 (1990), 1,832 (2000), 1,772 (2010), 1,767 (2020), 1,800 (2025); OECD average 1,736 (2025); 11 countries above the US in 2025, incl. Mexico 2,205, Chile 1,912, Greece 1,874, Israel 1,870, South Korea 1,833.

JILPT (OECD as of Aug 2025) US hours 1,880 (2000), 1,810 (2010), 1,800 (2020), 1,796 (2024); OECD warns the series is for comparing one country over time, not levels across countries; includes part-time workers.
US DOL: the FLSA 'does not require payment for time not worked, such as vacations'; vacation is a matter of agreement between employer and employee.

Israel's statutory minimum annual leave rose from 10 to 12 days from 1 Jan 2017, the first increase since 1951 (Annual Leave Law), rising with seniority from the fifth year; most OECD countries give 20 or more days.

OECD Family Database (Sept 2026): OECD average gap 10.1% in 2024, down 8.4 points since 2000; Israel among countries with gaps of 20% or more; Israel's data are monthly earnings, US weekly; US gap fell from the mid-1970s to early 2010s and little changed since 2014.

Shoresh (Ben-David and Kimhi), reported by JPost 4 Mar 2025: women's median monthly income in Israel was 76.9% of men's (2021–2023), a wider gap than in 35 of 38 OECD countries, and wider than 15 years earlier.
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): the gap widens after women have children while men's earnings rise after fatherhood (Ben-David and Kimhi)

us13_unions.topic: Histadrut vs US unions; density and bargaining coverage; laws; strikes

claims.text: BLS: US union membership rate 10.0% in 2025 (14.7m) vs 9.9% in 2024 (14.3m) and 20.1% (17.7m) in 1983; public sector 32.9%, private 5.9% (2025); 11.2% (16.5m) represented by unions; median weekly earnings $1,404 union vs $1,174 nonunion (full-time); October 2025 excluded owing to the shutdown.

Histadrut founded December 1920 in Haifa for Jewish workers; Arabs admitted from 1953 (Wikipedia; other accounts say 1959); owned Bank Hapoalim (lost after the 1983 bank-share crisis), ZIM and Clalit; employed about 280,000 in 1989; Clalit covered ~70% of Israelis in mid-1980s.

Histadrut density: 68% of the Jewish workforce (1927), ~75% (1939), ~85% of wage earners (1983), 27% of the workforce (2016); membership fell from 1.8m (~80% of the workforce) to about 200,000 in 1994–95 after the health law cut the Clalit link; ~650,000 (2005), 570,000 (2017); 800,000 per infobox; general strikes Feb 2012 and March 2023 (called off same day after Netanyahu paused the judicial legislation).

Shalev (1996): the Histadrut negotiated for 85% of wage earners until the early 1990s and spoke for about two-thirds of Israeli adults; it agreed to the 1985 stabilization plan; Labor lost control of it in May 1994; the National Health Insurance Law (early 1995) ended entitlement to Sick Fund care through membership.

OECD (Sept 2017, situation Dec 2015): Israel's private-sector union density 10–20%; collective bargaining coverage 20–30% of employees; bargaining predominantly company/sectoral, decentralised; extension of sectoral agreements by the ministry exists but is uncommon.

NPR, 2 Sept 2024: the Histadrut called a general strike after six hostages' bodies were recovered in Gaza; Ben Gurion airport paused flights for hours; Israel's Labor Court ordered it to end by 2:30 pm and the Histadrut complied.

Equitable Growth (2017): US bargaining is enterprise-level; the US ranked last of 21 OECD countries in collective bargaining coverage; nearly one in three US workers was a union member in 1960, just over one in ten in 2016.

Littler: Michigan's repeal of right-to-work took effect 30 Mar 2024 (first state in 58 years to repeal); 26 states have such laws under NLRA Section 14(b), which bar enforcement of union-security clauses.
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Netanyahu: 'Whoever murders hostages — does not want a deal'

us13_migrants.topic: Palestinian and migrant workers in Israel; unauthorized workers in the US

claims.text: PCBS: West Bank workers in Israel and settlements about 172,000 before the war (about 127,000 with permits), about 25,000 in Q4 2023, about 51,000 in Q4 2025 (about 14,000 permit holders); West Bank unemployment about 13% (Q3 2023) to about 28% (Q4 2025); Gaza unemployment about 45% before to about 68% (Q4 2024).

+972 (6 May 2026): over 200,000 Palestinians barred after 7 Oct 2023 (150,000 West Bank permit holders, ~50,000 without permits, 18,500 from Gaza); 8,000 permits in 2025; >10,000 work in settlements; residential construction fell 95%; Kav LaOved counts about 270,000 migrant workers; plans for ~65,000 from India, Sri Lanka and Uzbekistan; quotas ~30,000 each in agriculture and construction, caregiving uncapped; visas tied to the employer; agricultural migrants paid ~70% of wages owed (Kav LaOved 2014); Thai workers the group most affected on 7 Oct.

The Media Line citing PIBA: almost 61,000 new foreign-worker permits in 2025, total 227,044; a May 2024 government decision raised the quota to 3.3% of the population; PIBA's Moshe Nakash cited a shortfall of 100,000.

EPI citing Pew: 8.3 million unauthorized immigrants in the US labour force in 2022 (just under 5% of the workforce), up from 3.6 million in 1995; employers can use fear of retaliation and deportation to underpay them.
Contradiction: pre-war count of Palestinian workers in Israel differs: PCBS ~172,000 West Bank incl. ~127,000 permits; +972 150,000 permit holders + ~50,000 without; Media Line/Kav LaOved ~100,000.

Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): about 240,000 migrant workers (about 10% of the labour force) by 2000; at least three migrant workers killed by Iranian missiles in the 2026 war; 32 Thai workers killed and 22 taken hostage on 7 October 2023
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): the 8.3 million figure equals earlier peaks in 2008 and 2011
